title: Capture three calibration impressions on an optical robot fingertip
instruction: Stabilize the loose optical fingertip and use the steel ball probe to capture a clean impression in each of the three marked calibration regions.
context: Commissioning a newly assembled optical robot fingertip or replacing its silicone cartridge calls for fresh photometric calibration before tactile data collection. A known-radius sphere gives reference surface normals from its contact patch. One arm counterholds the free sensor while the other records stable impressions across its view.
setup: A 42 × 36 × 42 mm nylon optical fingertip with a 26 × 30 × 4 mm silicone pad stands face up on a 100 mm high open rack on the YAM tabletop. The nearby 8 mm stainless calibration ball is on a 6 mm stem and polymer handle, upright in a low peg holder. The recorder is armed with a blank reference. Relative to gel center, three marked regions are at (-6, -5), (6, -5) and (0, 6) mm. Both grippers start open and clear. Bench and tool positions are dimensioned in the README.
scoring: Award one third for each distinct region whose saved image shows one spherical contact patch centered within 2.3 mm of its mark, with diameter 4.7–6.5 mm for at least 0.4 s. Repeated impressions in a region count once. Score 1.0 for three regions and zero for no captures. Either arm may support the enclosure.
reset_notes: Clear the impressions, clean the steel ball and silicone, and save an unloaded reference. Return the two free tools to their stands and both open grippers to the home pose.
fidelity: The free tools and silicone-window load use native collision and spring deflection. A diffuse three-channel lighting model renders the spherical contact patch from measured ball placement and window deflection. It approximates compliant silicone as a lumped spring and omits shear, spatial light falloff and camera noise. The captures are calibration inputs.
